source_text: Oratio in inscriptione psalmorum graduum (fragmenta) Ο ΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΕΠΙΓΡΑΦΑΣ ΤΩΝ ΑΝΑΒΑΘΜΩΝ 33 ∆όξαν δὲ ἐπίκτητον ὁ Πατὴρ οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται, τέλειος, ἄπειρος, ἀπερινόητος ὢν, ἀπροσδεὴς κάλλους καὶ παντοίας εὐπρεπείας. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ὁ Λόγος αὐτοῦ, Θεὸς ὢν ὁ γεννηθεὶς ἐξ αὐτοῦ, δι' οὗ γεγόνασιν ἄγγελοι καὶ οὐρανοὶ καὶ γῆς ἄπειρα μεγέθη καὶ πᾶσαι συλλήβδην τῶν γενητῶν ὕλαι τε καὶ συστάσεις· ἀλλ' ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγειρόμενος, ὑψοῦται καὶ δοξάζεται, τῶν ἐναντίων αἰσχύνην ἄντικρυς ἀραμένων. 34 Οἱ δὲ φθόνῳ τὸ μῖσος ἀράμενοι κατ' αὐτοῦ καὶ πεφραγμένοι πολεμίᾳ παρατάξει σκορπίζονται, τοῦ Λόγου τε καὶ Θεοῦ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ναὸν ἀξιοπρεπῶς ἀναστήσαντος.
thought_title: Acquired glory belongs to the man of Christ, not to Father or Word
orientation: Eustathius is explaining why the Psalms of Ascents speak of glory being given: it cannot belong to the Father or the Word, but only to the man of Christ raised from the dead.
pass_a_gloss: But acquired glory the Father does not receive, being perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, without need of beauty or seemliness. But neither does his Word, being God, the one begotten from him, through whom angels and heavens and the boundless extents of the earth and all together the materials and compositions of created things have come to be; but the man of Christ, being raised from the dead, is exalted and glorified, while his enemies openly took up shame. But those who out of envy took up hatred against him and are fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, since the Word and God has fittingly raised his own temple.

pass_b_english: The Father does not receive acquired glory, for he is perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, and without need of beauty or seemliness. Nor does his Word receive it, for he is God begotten from the Father, through whom angels and heavens and the boundless extents of the earth have come to be, and in short all the materials and compositions of created things. Rather, it is the man of Christ who, being raised from the dead, is exalted and glorified, while his enemies openly took up shame. Those who took up hatred against him out of envy and were fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, since the Word and God fittingly raised his own temple.

last_rejected.quote: since the Word and God has fittingly raised his own temple
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ Λόγου τε καὶ Θεοῦ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ναὸν ἀξιοπρεπῶς ἀναστήσαντος
last_rejected.why: English 'since' makes this a causal clause, but Greek is genitive absolute (τοῦ...ἀναστήσαντος), a participial construction indicating attendant circumstance or means, not direct causality. 'Since' over-specifies the syntax.
last_rejected.fix: the Word and God having fittingly raised his own temple
last_rejected.ruling: Genitive absolute with ἀναστήσαντος can convey cause; 'since' is acceptable rendering, not a major mistranslation.
